title: Early-Life Exposure to Clostridium leptum Causes Pulmonary Immunosuppression.
ehr_evidence: The study utilized an experimental murine model using BALB/c mice delivered by caesarean section or vaginal delivery, with exposure to Clostridium leptum and ovalbumin allergen.
summary: Experimental study evaluating the impact of early-life Clostridium leptum exposure on asthma development, airway hyper-responsiveness, and pulmonary immune responses in a murine model.
key_findings: Early-life C. leptum feeding increased Treg cell frequency and number in caesarean-delivered mice compared to vaginally delivered mice.
C. leptum exposure significantly reduced airway hyper-responsiveness and BALF cell counts (eosinophils, neutrophils, lymphocytes, macrophages) in OVA-sensitized mice compared to controls.
Th1, Th2, Th9, and Th17 cell levels and associated cytokines were statistically decreased in C. leptum-exposed OVA-sensitized mice compared to OVA-sensitized controls (p < 0.05).
IL-10 and TGF-β1 levels were significantly higher in C. leptum-exposed OVA-sensitized mice compared to OVA-sensitized controls.
No significant difference in Th22 frequency or IL-22 production was observed between C. leptum-exposed and control OVA-sensitized groups.
limitations: murine model may not fully replicate human asthma pathophysiology
single bacterial strain and allergen model limits generalizability
data_availability_statement: All relevant data are within the paper.
